PhD in Bioinformatics Data Science
Home/Education/Degrees/PhD in Bioinformatics Data Science
A Ph.D. in Bioinformatics Data Science will train the next-generation of researchers and professionals who will play a key role in multi- and interdisciplinary teams, bridging life sciences and computational sciences. Students will receive training in experimental, computational and mathematical disciplines through their coursework and research. Students who complete this degree will be able to generate and analyze experimental data for biomedical research as well as develop physical or computational models of the molecular components that drive the behavior of the biological system.
The degree requires a minimum of 35 credits. Students must complete a minimum of 15 hours of coursework, plus 2 credit hours of seminar, 6 credit hours of research and 9 credit hours of doctoral dissertation (summarized in Table 1). Students who are admitted directly after a BS degree will be required to complete up to 9 additional credits in order to fulfill the core curriculum in the following areas: Programming, Statistics, and Life Science. In addition, if students entering the program with an MS degree are lacking equivalent required electives, they also will be required to complete courses in these three areas; however, these courses may fulfill the elective requirement in the PhD program, if approved in the program of study.
The program of study document can be found on the CBCB Graduate Resources page under the dropdown “Current Students - Most Commonly Used Forms.”
The curriculum information below is for students who matriculated in Fall 2026 or later. For students under the previous program of study, requirements can be viewed here and in the appropriate program of study on the Graduate Resources page.

Academic Load
Students in the Bioinformatics Data Science PhD program will typically complete the program in four to six years.
Students enrolled in at least 9 credit hours or in sustaining credit are considered full-time students. Those enrolled for fewer than 9 credit hours are considered part-time students, although students holding assistantships are considered full-time with 6 credits. Generally, a maximum load is 12 graduate credit hours; however, additional credit hours may be taken with the approval of the student's advisor and the Graduate College. A maximum course load in either summer or winter session is 7 credit hours. Permission must be obtained to carry an overload in any session.
Grade Requirements
Grades of B or higher in the core and required electives courses to be eligible to continue in the program. Students receiving a B- or lower in a required core course are subject to dismissal from the program. However, students may file an appeal to the Bioinformatics Data Science Graduate Committee for approval to retake a course and remain in the program. Students must obtain at least a 3.0 cumulative grade point average to be eligible for the degree.

Formation of Graduate Committee
The student needs to establish a Dissertation Committee within the first year of study. The Committee should consist of at least four faculty members, including the primary faculty advisor (serving as the Committee Chair), a secondary faculty advisor (in a complementary field to the primary advisor), a second faculty from the home department, and one CBCB affiliate faculty outside the Departments of the primary and secondary advisors or from outside the University. Students must complete the Dissertation Committee Formation form and submit to the Academic Advisor.
Students should convene their dissertation committee at least once per year.
The Preliminary Exam
The preliminary examination assesses three key areas: 1) fundamental knowledge of the topics relevant to your program of study, 2) ability to communicate science, and 3) ability to apply scientific reasoning skills.
The exam should be scheduled before the end of the fourth semester and will consist of an oral exam in subjects based on the Bioinformatics Data Science core courses.* In recognition of the importance of the core curriculum in providing a good test of the student’s knowledge, students must achieve a minimum 3.0 GPA in the core curriculum before taking the preliminary exam. Students will not be permitted to take the preliminary examination if the core grade requirements and cumulative GPA of 3.0 has not been achieved.
Format. The exam will be administered by a Preliminary Examination Committee, consisting of one instructor from each of the three core courses in their Program of Study. The student will be responsible for identifying and scheduling a mutually convenient 2 hour block of time for the exam. During the exam, the committee will ask the student to discuss and answer questions regarding various topics relevant to the core course content. The goal of this examination is to evaluate the student’s ability to retain, discuss, and apply important concepts and skills from the core courses. Students are NOT expected to prepare a presentation for the exam and will NOT be allowed the use of notes.
Preparation. Students are responsible for reviewing the concepts from each of their core courses to prepare for the exam. If a student can no longer access the course materials in Canvas, they should contact their instructor to reactivate access. In addition to simply reviewing the content of the course, students should give careful consideration to how concepts can be applied to research. The Bioinformatics Student Association (BiSA) maintains preparation materials for the preliminary examination. Once enrolled in their final core course, students should contact the BiSA Officers (bisa-officers@udel.edu) to request access to these resources.
Results. At the end of the examination, the Committee will immediately confer and agree upon a single outcome determination. This outcome will be discussed with the student and submitted via the Results of Preliminary Exam Form to the Graduate Program Director. Possible outcomes:
Unconditional Pass. The student has successfully demonstrated knowledge and may proceed to the next stage of his/her degree training.
Conditional pass. The Examination Committee judges the student to have an overall solid grasp of the core material, but identified one or more specific areas in need of additional reinforcement. The Examination Committee will communicate the conditional pass to the student and provide specific requirements, guidelines, and expected timeframe for completing the condition. The student must inform the Examination Committee when they have completed the requested conditions. The Examination Committee will then determine whether all recommendations have been satisfactorily completed and will either 1) inform the Student and Graduate Program Director that the conditions have been completed or 2) order a re-examination.
Re-examination. In the event that the committee feels that the student displayed significant deficiencies in multiple areas of knowledge a re-examination may be ordered. The re-examination will be done using the same format as the original exam and must be scheduled prior to the beginning of the next academic semester, unless otherwise permitted by the Graduate Program Director. The Examination Committee may grant only a single re-examination for each student. Successful re-examinations may result in Conditional or Unconditional Pass outcomes, however if the student does not perform satisfactorily the Examination Committee is required to record a Failure outcome.
Failure. This outcome would indicate that the Examination Committee considers the student incapable of completing degree training. The student’s academic progress will be reviewed by the Graduate Affairs Committee, who will make recommendations to the Program Director regarding the student’s enrollment status. The Program Director may recommend to the Graduate College that the student be dismissed from the Program immediately.
*Students who need to complete prerequisite courses may request a deadline extension for the preliminary and subsequently the candidacy examination. Requests must be submitted to the Graduate Program Committee prior to the start of the third semester.
The Candidacy Exam
The candidacy examination must be completed by the end of the sixth semester of enrollment. It requires a formal, detailed, written proposal be submitted to the Dissertation Committee and an oral defense of the student’s proposed research project. There is no required format for the written proposal, though the document must adhere to typical conventions of scholarly and scientific writing. The written proposal should be submitted to the Committee two weeks before the oral defense. The oral defense is a closed meeting between the student and members of the Committee. The student will be responsible for identifying and scheduling a mutually convenient 2 hour block of time for the exam.
Upon the recommendation of the Dissertation Committee, the student may be admitted to candidacy for the PhD degree. The stipulations for admission to doctoral candidacy are that the student has (i) completed one academic year of full-time graduate study in residence at the University of Delaware, (ii) completed all required courses with the exception of BINF865 and BINF969, (iii) passed the preliminary exam, (iv) demonstrated the ability to perform research, and (v) had a research project accepted by the Dissertation Committee. Within one week of the candidacy exam, complete and submit the Recommendation for Candidacy for Doctoral Degree form to the Academic Advisor.
The Dissertation Exam
The dissertation examination of the PhD program will involve the approval of the written dissertation and an oral defense of the candidate’s dissertation. The written dissertation will be submitted to the Dissertation Committee at least three weeks in advance of the oral defense date. The oral defense date will be publicly announced at least two weeks prior to the scheduled date. The oral presentation will be open to the public and all members of the Bioinformatics Data Science program. The public presentation is immediately followed by a closed session between the student and the Dissertation Committe, in which the student is further examined on the contents of their presentation and written dissertation, and lastly a private deliberation of the Committee. The Dissertation Committee will approve the candidate’s dissertation. The student and the primary faculty advisor will be responsible for making all corrections to the dissertation document and for meeting all Graduate College deadlines. Within one week of the dissertation defense, complete and submit the Certification of Doctoral Dissertation Defense Form to the Academic Advisor.
